co_better_than_love.descent_text: The route ends on the summit, so the walk-off starts at the top of the peak. From the top, follow the summit ridge east along the crest, tracking the cairns, until you reach the end of the last big buttress, where bolted anchors mark the first rappel; the station sits on the nose of the buttress and is easy to miss. Parties typically make two short rappels, and a single 60 m rope generally reaches the first. Below them, scramble down a gully, then work back across to a second gully and follow cairned third and fourth class ground through trees to the foot of the cliff. Avoid the big gully farther east, which is loose and harder than it appears.
co_better_than_love.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and take the trail to Emerald Lake (roughly 1.7 to 1.8 miles one way). Go around the left side of the lake, scramble through talus, and pick up a climbers' trail beneath the wall. Better Than Love is on the Second Buttress, the middle of the three; from the foot of the buttress, step up and left from the Love Route and Culp-Bossier starts to a grassy shelf beside the giant corner. Snow often lingers at the foot of the face early in the season.
